question: On 8 December 2023, a Liberian flagged vessel lost a cargo of millions of microplastic pellets off the Portuguese coast. This cargo has reached the Galician coast and represents a serious problem for my country’s coast, fisheries and marine fauna, with very serious and obvious environmental and economic consequences.

Although it was aware of the exact date of the release of plastic pellets and their movement towards the Galician coast, the Galician regional Government concealed the polluting accident and initially failed to inform the affected fisheries of the details of the spill or its serious consequences.

It also failed to activate the anti-pollution protocol from the outset, so that the pollution spread in an uncontrolled manner; had it done so, the consequences that ensued would have been avoided. 1.

Are the Commission and the European Maritime Safety Agency aware of the delayed implementation of anti-pollution protocols by the Galician Government and of the failure to comply with European maritime safety legislation?

Does the Commission know that this delay led to a much greater environmental problem that would have been minimised had the anti-pollution protocol been triggered and implemented from the outset? What action does the Commission intend to take?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.4.2024) The European maritime safety legislation does not include national or regional anti-pollution protocols. As a consequence, the Commission is not informed about their operation and is not aware of the dates of the implementation of the Galician regional government’s anti-pollution protocol in relation to the pollution incident in question.

The Member States involved (Portugal and Spain) may carry out an investigation in line with Directive 2009/18/EC establishing the fundamental principles governing the investigation of accidents in the maritime transport sector1. However, to date, the Commission is not aware of any such action taken.

The Commission is nevertheless aware of the negative environmental impact that the incident has had on the Galician coast. The action on plastic pellets that the Commission proposes is the proposal for a Regulation on preventing plastic pellet losses2 adopted in October 2023. It is currently under examination by the co-legislators and international shipping of plastic pellets is among the topics discussed.

Directive 2009/18/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 April 2009 establishing the fundamental principles governing the investigation of accidents in the maritime transport sector and amending Council Directive 1999/35/EC and Directive 2002/59/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (OJ L 131, 28.5.2009, p. 114). 2 https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/12823-Microplastics-pollutionmeasures-to-reduce-its-impact-on-the-environment_en 1
